# dsh-balance-indicator
**English** · Русский
**A DeepSeek Harness plugin that shows your account balance and the spend of the current session in
the composer dock, next to the built-in token and cache pills.**
DSH 0.2.x, MIT. Spec: `remote.account.getBalance`, slot `conversation.composer.dock`.
The row looks like this:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

- **A grid, not a flow.** The row is a CSS grid of four content columns plus two service ones: the
c

oin, the label, one column per currency, the `Session` label and its value. A dollar sits strictly
u

nder a dollar and a yuan under a yuan, and the two rows' labels start on the same vertical. There
ar

e no ` + ` or ` · ` separators — the alignment itself is the separator.
- **The marker on the left**

is the `💰` emoji in its own column, at `17px`, centred across both rows.
Its size is set explicitly

rather than inherited, because emoji glyphs ignore the parent's line box.
17px was picked from rend

ered variants (bag at 13px and 17px, coin, banknote, card, bank, the text
`¥$`, the sign `¤`, drawn

SVG circles with `¥` and `$`): clearly bigger than before, without
competing with the figures.
- **C

urrency order** comes from the `Topped-up` row (descending); currencies that exist only in the
grant

ed balance are appended after it. Both rows share the order — otherwise the columns would not
line u

p.
- **`Topped-up:`** is the topped-up balance (`normal_wallets`). If every currency rounds to `0.00

0`,
the largest one is shown: a zero balance is information, an empty string is not.
- **`Granted:`*

* is the granted balance (`bonus_wallets`). The row appears **only when it is
non-empty**: no grante

d funds (or they round to `0.000`) means no row and no label, while the
[该节后续省略]
## Checks
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## Status: works

Verified in the live GUI (DSH 0.2.0-rc.2): the row renders in the composer dock and shows the
balanc

e — at the time of that check `💰 $0.76 — $0.00 session` (USD account; the separator and the
layout h
ave changed since, see above).

The main trap that kept the row stuck on `…`: in a client plugin you **must declare the namespaced
s
ervice**, not just the root one. This works:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

With only `'remote'`, `ctx.remote.account.getBalance(...)` goes out and never gets an answer —
loadi
ng forever. The shipped `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-chat` does the same for `remote.session`.

The second fix, which takes effect after a DSH restart (the ESM module is cached): the host half
dec

lares `export const inject = ['deepseekAccount']` — without it, touching the service in Cordis
throw
s and the diagnostic beacon stops after the first line.
## When the balance refreshes
| Trigger | Condition |

| Plugin activation | Once, on page load |
| One early retry after 2 s | If the **first** read faile

d (waiting for the account namespace) |
| **Every 15 seconds** | A steady interval while the tab is

open |
| Clicking `↻` | Manually, at any time |
| `F5` | Anew on mount |
The refresh is **deliberately not tied to agent turns**: a turn can last for minutes, and reading at
its end would leave the figure stale for exactly that long. The loop runs strictly on a timer.

Overlapping requests are excluded: while the previous read has not finished, the next tick is
skippe

d. That matters because the interval (15 s) is shorter than one request's timeout (20 s) —
without t
he guard, requests would pile up on every stall.

Rate: one request every 15 seconds, i.e. **4 per minute** and ~5760 per day per open tab. DSH does
n

ot cache the balance: every read is a real `GET
https://platform.deepseek.com/api/v0/users/get_user_

summary` with the account token. On error the row
shows `💰 !` with the reason, and the next tick tri

with the account token. On error the row
shows `💰 !` with the reason, and the next tick tries again.
## What "spent this session" really means
DSH has **no monetary spend accounting**: only the account balance (with currencies) and token usage
(`tokenUsage`: uncached input / output / cache read / cache write). So the second part of the row i

s
the **balance difference** from the first successful read on this page to now.
The baseline is taken **at the first read**, not the first render: the composer dock may mount after
page load, and anchoring to the render would lose the spend accumulated before the chat was opened.
It is kept in `sessionStorage` — **one key per wallet** (`topped:CNY`, `granted:USD`, …), so a page
reload does not reset it.

Every wallet needs a baseline because Platform does not necessarily charge the session to the
topped

-up balance: on an account with granted funds the spend may come out of those, and the topped-up
bal

ance then stands still. The session figure used to be tied to "the largest currency" — and if the
la

rger one was the granted wallet, which had no baseline, `Session` froze at `0.000` for the whole
ses

sion. Now the figure follows the wallet whose change is larger in absolute value, and the tooltip
na
mes it (`Session: ¥1.910 — Granted CNY`).
Consequence: if another session or window is spending in parallel, its spend lands in this differenc

e
too. The tooltip's label reflects that.
## Where the data comes from

- Client half: RPC `ctx.remote.account.getBalance({ version, locale, timezoneOffsetSeconds })` →
`{

ok: true, value: { status, value: [{ currency, balance }], bonusWallets: [...] } }`, `null` when
not

signed in.
- Host half: `ctx.deepseekAccount` → `GET https://platform.deepseek.com/api/v0/users/get

_user_summary`
with the `x-dsh-auth-token` header (the token stays on the host and never reaches the

browser).
- Currencies: `CNY`, `USD`. Granted wallets (`bonus_wallets`) go into the `Granted:` grou

p, and in the
tooltip with currency codes next to the amounts.
## Where it sits in the UI
Slot `conversation.composer.dock` (list, session-scope, "Ambient entries below the composer card").

The shipped entry is `StatsPills` from `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-chat` with `id: 'stats'`,
`order:

0`. This plugin uses `id: 'balance-indicator'`, `order: 1000`: lists are sorted by `priority`,
then
by `order` **ascending**, so the block comes last and replaces nothing.
**The limit of what is possible.** To the right of the dock in the same line sits the context meter
(`ContextMeter`, the "43%"), and the composer renders it **after** the slot, not inside it:
[该节后续省略]
